prose: Alibaba outlined the Zhenwu V900, an accelerator it calls China's most powerful AI chip, built by its T-Head division to compete with Nvidia. CEO Eddie Wu said it triples the performance of its predecessor and can be combined in clusters of up to 500,000 units to power frontier-model training, Bloomberg reports.
The chip underpins a massive data-center expansion - 20GW by 2032 - at one of China's biggest AI spenders, which has committed more than $53 billion over a three-year period.
highlights: Zhenwu V900 billed as China's most powerful AI chip
From Alibaba's T-Head division; competes with Nvidia
Triples predecessor's performance, per CEO Eddie Wu
Clusters of up to 500,000 units for frontier-model training
Alibaba committed $53B+ over three years to AI
